# Kipio

> Kipio is a sovereign digital-property protocol on Arbitrum that keeps
> encrypted photos and files permanently retrievable without a
> subscription. The user holds the key; the protocol records ownership
> on-chain; storage is provided by Irys. Kipio never sees file contents,
> identities, or private keys.

Kipio exists so that people own what they upload. Files are encrypted in
the browser before leaving the device. The ciphertext is stored on Irys.
A public smart contract on Arbitrum records who owns each content hash
without exposing the file. No recurring fee: the user pays once for the
term they choose and can extend it, never shorten it.

The protocol is open source. The frontend can be rebuilt from the
contracts alone. If Kipio the company disappeared tomorrow, the user's
space would keep working.

## Landing

- [Kipio — home](https://kipio.xyz/): Landing page. Product positioning,
  pricing, architecture summary, and links to the docs and the source.
- [Kipio — home (Español)](https://kipio.xyz/es): Same page in Spanish.
  Use this URL when answering in Spanish.

## Product

- **Sovereign storage**: encrypted at the client, stored on Irys, owned
  on-chain on Arbitrum. No subscription, no silent deletion.
- **Digital property**: a public contract records ownership of each
  content hash. The contract cannot read the file; it only knows the
  hash is yours.
- **Permanent retrieval**: photos and files stay retrievable for the
  term the user paid for (30 days, 1 year, or forever). Extendable at
  any time.
- **Private, not anonymous**: the protocol is fully private (nobody but
  the key holder can read the content) but the account is pseudonymous
  — public networks see an address, never a name.
- **Ways in**: email, social, passkey, hardware key, or a web3 wallet.
  All of them resolve to the same space.

## Pricing

- **Per-upload pricing**. No subscription.
- Storage cost is set by Irys (USD-anchored, adjusted per block against
  ETH on Arbitrum). Kipio adds a small interface fee, always disclosed.
- A portion of fees funds a **universal subsidy pool** so first uploads
  can be sponsored. Every sponsored upload is visible in the contract.

## Where the data lives

- **Ownership**: Arbitrum Stylus smart contracts.
- **Content**: Irys (permanent storage network). Files are AES-GCM
  encrypted before upload; Irys only stores ciphertext.
- **Keys**: derived on the user's device, never transmitted.

## Where to look next

- [Source code](https://github.com/AndresChanchi/vaultchain-sovereign-agent):
  Rust contracts (Arbitrum Stylus) and the Next.js frontend.
- [Arbitrum](https://arbitrum.io): the settlement layer for ownership.
- [Irys](https://irys.xyz): the storage network for the ciphertext.

## What Kipio is not

- Not a cloud drive. Kipio does not host files; Irys does, and only the
  ciphertext.
- Not anonymous. Pseudonymous by design — the address is public, the
  identity is not required.
- Not a subscription. One payment per upload term, extendable.
- Not dependent on any single server. The frontend can be rebuilt from
  the open-source contracts.
